summary: Weekly POC sync focused on KV/prefix cache hit rates and prompt reuse strategies. Reviewed last week's metrics (avg KV hit 42%, prefix reuse ~18%), identified tuning knobs for eviction and prefetch, agreed on a 48-hour high-fidelity run and follow-up security meeting.
transcript:
HEADER: 2025-10-21 15:30 UTC | Duration 42m | Attendees: Eli Navarro (Redwood), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Tom Adler (Clarion CTO), Rina Lopez (Clarion ML Eng), Markus Chen (Clarion SRE), Asha Kumar (Product)

00:00 Tom Adler: okay everyone, thanks for making time, it's our weekly POC sync for Clarion caching work. Can we kick off?
00:08 Eli Navarro: Yep, thanks Tom. Quick agenda: recap last week metrics, Priya will walk tuning recs, then action items and the 48-hour production-like run.
00:17 Rina Lopez: Quick note — we had a mid-week job that spiked latency, I dug in a bit, will share logs.
00:22 Priya Desai: cool, i'll start with the numbers we pulled from the dashboard. Apologies, some of the labels got munged in the export.
00:30 Priya Desai: so top-line, KV hit around 42% across the traffic sample, prefix reuse about 18% when we consider exact prompt matches. We also saw a long tail of low-frequency prompts — that is the usual.
00:48 Jordan Li: to add, when we included the near-match prefix logic (prefix fuzz ~0.8) hit rate rose to about 51% but at the cost of some misaligned responses, so quality regression tradeoff.
01:02 Tom Adler: that 51% sounds great but what was the quality delta? any measurable downstream regression?
01:10 Priya Desai: subjective evals showed minor alignment drift on 4% of samples, automated BLEU/ROUGE style checks aren't great for chat but we flagged those. We'll surface concrete examples.
01:25 Rina Lopez: i saw a couple where the model pulled a wrong section — felt like the cached reply came from different context. Could be prefix inflation.
01:34 Eli Navarro: that's expected when you loosen prefix matching. We should balance hit-rate improvements with a more conservative accept threshold and maybe a second-stage verification for critical intents.
01:44 Markus Chen: from SRE side, that spike i mentioned earlier correlated with cache eviction storms — bursts of many small unique prompts causing evictions and higher I/O.
01:55 Priya Desai: ok that suggests we tune eviction policy — we recommended LRU with a small frequency bias, but we can add a short grace TTL for recently seen keys to avoid rapid churn.
02:06 Tom Adler: can you elaborate on grace TTL? what's the magnitude?
02:09 Priya Desai: like 30s to 2m depending on traffic — small enough to avoid staleness, long enough to ride the burst so you don't evict then immediately reload.
02:19 Rina Lopez: for our burst profile i think 45s might be good, we have spikes that are about 1m in 90th percentile.
02:26 Jordan Li: also worth enabling prefix prefetch for flows that hit certain intents — if we detect intent A, prefetch top-N candidate prefixes into memory. That boosted our internal hit rate on a similar customer by ~12%.
02:40 Tom Adler: prefetch sounds promising, but what's the cost impact? more memory and potentially wasteful loads?
02:47 Priya Desai: yes it's a tradeoff — memory and token cost to prefetch. But you can restrict prefetch to high-value intents only. We'll provide config snippets.
02:57 Eli Navarro: i'll just flag that prefetch in Dedicated mode is cheaper per-token than Hosted at high scale because of reserved capacity and better tail latency. I can share the delta after the call.
03:06 Markus Chen: curious about our observed prefix reuse 18% — is that per session or global?
03:11 Priya Desai: it's global across all users in the sample. When we isolate high-volume endpoints reuse goes up to ~35%.
03:20 Rina Lopez: i'll attach the endpoint map in the deck — some low-volume endpoints skew the global number down.
03:27 Eli Navarro: good. Next, auto-eviction thresholds — we suggested keeping small keys for 100MB total and use a size-weighted LRU. Did Clarion try that config?
03:37 Markus Chen: we replicated the size-weighted LRU overnight. It helped a bit, but we still saw small key churn. The debug logs show many tiny keys from telemetry and micro interactions.
03:47 Priya Desai: can you filter telemetry from caching layer? We recommend not caching ephemeral telemetry prompts and only caching user-visible completions.
03:56 Rina Lopez: yep we can do that on the client side, will add a flag to skip caching for telemetry.
04:03 Tom Adler: question on prompt reuse strategy — should we canonicalize prompts? We have slight template variations that block reuse.
04:12 Jordan Li: canonicalization is high ROI. Normalizing whitespace, removing session IDs, and tokenizing stable template slots increases reuse. We also use a light fingerprinting step that preserves semantics.
04:24 Rina Lopez: we were worried about losing critical slot info, how reversible is canonicalization for debugging?
04:30 Priya Desai: we keep original payloads in logs for auditing; canonicalization is only for the cache key pipeline so you can always map back.
04:36 Tom Adler: good.
04:40 Eli Navarro: quick aside — there's some noise in the transcript exports where K/V is written as K V — ignore that in the doc.
04:47 Markus Chen: ha, yep saw that.
04:50 Priya Desai: next slide — prefetch candidate selection. We suggest a top-10 per-intent prefetch list derived from the last 7 days of traffic and updated daily. For Clarion, that yields a focused prefetch set without overfilling memory.
05:08 Rina Lopez: top-10 sounds reasonable. Is it static or adaptive?
05:11 Jordan Li: adaptive — it can slide window and decay older candidates. You can also pin critical ones.
05:18 Tom Adler: what's the instrumentation we need to validate prefetch benefits?
05:21 Priya Desai: metrics: prefetch hit rate, downstream latency reduction for prefetched flows, and cost delta on memory/tokens. We'll propose a dashboard template.
05:30 Eli Navarro: about the 48-hour run — Clarion will do a production-like replay to our test cluster. Key success metric is sustained KV hit > 48% and tail p95 latency under 350ms. Anything to add?
05:42 Rina Lopez: also looking at correctness: less than 1% incorrect reuse where cached reply mismatches intent.
05:50 Markus Chen: we can capture traces and full request/response for a sample. We'll redact PII before sharing.
06:00 Tom Adler: good. On security, Asha has a few compliance asks. Asha?
06:06 Asha Kumar: yes, Clarion's legal wants the KMS flow diagram and SSO integration steps. Also an audit log retention question — can we increase retention for this pilot?
06:18 Eli Navarro: yes, we can share the KMS diagram. For audit logs, retention is configurable depending on plan; for the POC we can extend retention to 90 days. We'll send the docs.
06:30 Asha Kumar: great — also need confirmation we don't persist raw PII in the cache.
06:36 Priya Desai: we don't recommend caching raw PII. We'll provide a scrub/transform pattern and a config example to enforce redaction at the edge.
06:46 Tom Adler: excellent. Back to tuning: eviction grace TTL + prefetch + canonicalization, any other quick wins?
06:53 Jordan Li: batching strategy — larger continuous batching helps throughput but can hurt latency for single-turn queries. We proposed dynamic batch sizing: prioritize single-turn low-latency with small batches, and use larger batching for queued workloads.
07:09 Markus Chen: is dynamic batching plug-and-play or does it need model changes?
07:13 Priya Desai: runtime supports it; it's a config knob per route. We'll include recommended thresholds.
07:20 Rina Lopez: can you share those thresholds? our 95th percentile latency budget is 500ms so we need to be careful.
07:27 Priya Desai: absolutely. For your profile, small-batch target size should be 1-4 tokens and fluid scaling up to 16 for background jobs.
07:36 Eli Navarro: quick Q from logs — some of the cached kv keys had a TTL of zero due to misconfig on client. Did you fix that?
07:44 Markus Chen: yes, that was a bug in our client lib; we patched and rolled yesterday.
07:49 Tom Adler: nice.
07:51 Priya Desai: ok, let's surface the exact config we recommend: 1) canonicalize keys (normalize templates), 2) size-weighted LRU + grace TTL 45s, 3) top-10 adaptive prefetch for high-value intents, 4) enable KV debug during 48h run, 5) filter telemetry from cache. We'll email the YAML.
08:12 Rina Lopez: can you remind on how to enable debug logs without massive overhead?
08:16 Jordan Li: enable sporadic sampling — 1% at normal, 100% for flagged endpoints. That gives signal while keeping storage down.
08:24 Tom Adler: i have a procurement question — if we need Dedicated for this workload what's the lead time?
08:29 Eli Navarro: typically 2-3 weeks for Dedicated provisioning in your region; we can prioritize. Pricing delta i'll send today.
08:36 Asha Kumar: also need SOC2 attestation doc for our security team.
08:40 Eli Navarro: yes we'll attach that.
08:43 Priya Desai: last technical call item: when we loosen prefix fuzz, add a second-stage intent classifier to vet high-risk matches. That's a cheap safety net.
08:55 Rina Lopez: can the classifier run in background for prefetched results?
08:59 Jordan Li: yes, or as an in-line microservice depending on latency budget. We'll provide both patterns.
09:06 Tom Adler: timeline check — we'll run the 48h test starting Monday 2025-10-27, is that feasible?
09:12 Markus Chen: yes, we'll prepare infra and send credentials.
09:16 Eli Navarro: great. Any blockers?
09:18 Rina Lopez: i just need the canonicalization sample and the prefetch extractor script.
09:22 Priya Desai: we'll push both to the shared drive by Friday 2025-10-24.
09:27 Tom Adler: okay sounds like we have clear next steps.
09:30 Eli Navarro: quick recap then action items — Priya will share tuned config, Rina will send top prefixes, Markus will enable KV debug, Eli will share pricing & docs.
09:42 Asha Kumar: can you also include the KMS flow and audit retention in that packet?
09:47 Eli Navarro: yes.
09:50 Tom Adler: thanks everyone. We'll reconvene after the 48-hour run — target review meeting 2025-10-29.
09:59 Eli Navarro: thanks all.
10:02 (call ends)
